notes.title: iMPORTANT TIPS FOR PLAYING OUR DEMO!
notes.content:
[b]Important Tips for Playing the Ringleaders Demo in Next Fest[/b]

-You need[b] 4 players [/b]to start a game.

-Once a game starts, no one else can hop into your session.

-You will not get matched with players who are not in the same region as you (so even if you’re using a friend’s room code, but your region isn’t the same, you won’t get into their session). You can adjust your region in settings => gameplay

-This is our demo, so we expect there to be some bugs. Please send your logs by going to  settings => support => report. 

[b]-Don't forget to claim your FREE HAT! [/b]

[b]LIST OF KNOWN ISSUES[/b]

- Dead agents (ghosts) can become jittery on rare occasions due to - latency
- Health bar disappears when cloaked
- Rarely a player model can be missing in postgame
- Lower quality settings affects UI resolution

notes.title: Dev Diary #4: Creating Stylized Explosion VFX in Unity!
notes.content:
Our VFX specialist wrote this blog on stylized explosions! You can read the full article and view the images he is referencing here: 

[url=https://www.artstation.com/blogs/ryanbradford/Wojz/creating-stylized-explosion-vfx-in-unity]Dev's take on stylized VFX in Unity[/url]


Creating Stylized Explosion VFX in Unity!
Ryan Bradford

Welcome!

Stylized games have seen a massive surge to the forefront of the gaming industry, and it just so happens that I am working on one! 

Ringleaders 

In this post I will explain the way that I approach an effect like this, how you might apply some artistic principles to your own, and some general tips at the end for the unity particle system.

Here's a look at the explosion I'll be referencing throughout this post: 

The Boom
What is the most important part of the explosion? The BOOM! So, first things first, it is important to understand how you want your boom to appear. Looking at a conventional explosion we can break it up into a couple of sections:

The explosion is initiated
This can be any sort of signal or implication that a blast is about to happen. In the example, a mine is placed and then begins activating. It is important to use this to telegraph to the player what is about to happen so they know to run! This section can be anything from a couple of particles being sucked into the center, to an entire pre-explosion animation sequence.

The Sun Phase
If you look closely you can see that right at the start of the explosion there is the most intense color and heat.

This should be communicated through your initial particle burst. Typically this is made up of a bright flash followed by a ball of the brightest/most intense color you want present in the effect. It's important that the Sun Phase only lasts a moment* so that the rest of the explosion can play out.
* -- This is how traditional explosions work, and by no means are you limited to keeping this short if your explosion should be slowed down or last longer than usual.
The BOOM
Now comes the blast! Here we get the typical smoke cloud and explosion of debris that you find in most grenade and bomb effects. I feel this is the best place for artistic expression because this phase typically lasts a second or two and is easily visible during run time. In a stylized effect, it can be fun to make up shapes that your smoke cloud takes on, create layering with multiple clouds, and use colors that typically aren't found in real life explosions. In the example above you can see we're using a noise texture on our expanding spheres of post Sun Phase smoke. Additionally we've layered multiple effects to create a shadow cloud that generates a lot of contrast with the larger red cloud.
 
Some good options for play here can be to change the shape of your expanding mesh or try different color combinations (vibrating colors are a great place to start!). 
The Particles
Now that we have covered the basic approach, it's time to discuss how to actually get there. The Unity particle system is pretty intricate, and I would highly recommend you take a look at it before continuing because particles can be tricky little goobers. Some other great resources are Gabriel Aguiar and VFX Apprentice.

One more thing before you go deeper, it would be wise to brush up on your photoshop skills at this point. The particles are where an understanding of 2D painting and technical know-how come together.

Now then, on to the particles. As you begin with the pre-existing Unity particle system, there are a couple of useful effects that deliver a lot of impact. The first of these is the size over lifetime effect. This allows you to directly tie the scale of your object to a curve that is driven by the lifetime value of your particles. With a curve like this, you can achieve common animation principles like squash and stretch easily. Additionally, you can split the size over lifetime into separate axes allowing for more explicit control over dimensions. Here's an example of one of my own curves I like to use: 

The second useful setting on the particle effects that will help create your explosions is the color over lifetime effect. This does the same thing as size over lifetime but for color! Together these two can be used to exaggerate your particles main effects, or create very subtle tertiary particles that support the main effect. Hand in hand, these two will go a long way to making your particle effects look and feel more alive and professional.

Materials & Shadergraph
The use of materials and shaders could be their own post entirely (and likely will be!) so I will keep this section brief. The most important thing to know here is the use of basic shader graph functions. Things like scrolling textures, screen space rendering, and timers are incredibly useful, and should not be underestimated when considering how to approach an effect. Many effects can forgo particles altogether if they make clever use of animators and a well made material. That being said, it is useful to know that for the explosion in our demonstration above, I made use of one important node that you will all find useful when creating many things. 

The Voronoi node is a simple math based noise that is seriously useful. It is found just about everywhere these days, from textures made in Substance Designer, to procedural terrain generation in voxel games. Voronoi is definitely something that should be in your artist's toolbelt from here on out. Use it to create the wavy shell of the explosion like I did above, or use it to create a wood grain by stretching your UV's, you can even use it to make stylized tornadoes. No matter what effect you're considering, a useful noise texture can be what it takes to push it that extra mile. 

In Conclusion
I hope you learned something useful! As I previously mentioned, this post is meant to be an introductory exploration into creating stylized effects. So, hopefully you have gained some knowledge that can be applied to your future effects! Thank you so much for taking the time to read this, and please do reach out if you have any questions. Have a great day :)

notes.title: Now Accepting Applications to the Ringleaders Playtester Program
notes.content:
We’re excited to announce the Ringleaders Playtester Program! 

Over the next few months as we approach our Early Access launch, we’ll be hosting regular group-style playtests. You can apply to be a part of this core group [url=https://forms.gle/VVJZQiWjecoRfwnA9]here[/url].

Benefits of becoming a playtester:
[list]
[*][b]Direct access to the devs - [/b]During playtests, you’ll join a group of our developers and be able to ask questions, give suggestions and feedback, and have a say in the development process.
[*][b]Invitations to secret Discord channels - [/b]Our playtester channels are reserved exclusively for players who’ve dedicated time to providing us feedback, bashing bugs, and helping improve the game.
[*][b]In-game rewards -[/b] We’re still finalizing the details, but we plan to reward playtesters with in-game rewards, unique cosmetics, and special Discord roles and privileges. Stay tuned; there’s more to come!
[*][b]The chance to shape the game - [/b]We want to make a game that our players love, so this is a unique opportunity to share your ideas and come up with fun features and suggestions that we can incorporate into our development roadmap.
[/list]

If you’re looking to start a career in gaming and want to get an inside look at what it’s like to develop an indie game, or if you’re just a passionate gamer looking to provide feedback on an early product, the [b]Ringleaders Playtester Program[/b] is for you!

notes.title: Ringleaders has been selected to participate in Steam’s SHMUP Fest
notes.content:
We’re excited to announce that Ringleaders will be participating in Steam’s SHMUP Fest, which runs from September 25 - October 2. We’re merging tense and chaotic shoot ‘em up gameplay with social deduction mechanics—join the fight.

[previewyoutube=uqd1a0xJuoQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]What is Ringleaders?
[/h2]Work together with up to 8 teammates to fight your way through the retro-futuristic city of Carillon, while carrying out the orders of Aurora, leader of the Cyphers. You’ll have to smuggle precious Luminos tonic, destroy enemy stockpiles, and rescue hostages, all while fending off the sentries of the NERVOS corporation.

Not only are the agents of NERVOS out to stop you at every turn, they’ll also offer impressive sums of money to reward Cyphers who turn against their own team. With trust as your most valuable and vulnerable asset, tread carefully in a world where friends can quickly become foe in the blink of an eye. Will you collaborate with your fellow Cyphers, or will you become an informant for NERVOS?

[h2]When can I play the game?
[/h2]We haven’t announced an official launch date yet, but we’re now hosting regular playtests for select individuals who want to be among the first to play Ringleaders and provide feedback to help shape the game. 

[h2]What can I expect from our playtester program?
[/h2]Become an extension of our game dev team! Join playtests, provide recommendations, suggestions, report bugs, and co-create Ringleaders with us. 

We’re currently accepting applications for playtesters. Submit your interest [url=https://forms.gle/bNqwuiA7fbddx4aK9]here[/url].

[h2]How can I stay up to date on development?
[/h2]We’re actively sharing our development journey on social media. For the most up to date information, join our [url=https://discord.gg/JScb6EVN8g]Discord[/url], follow us on [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@playringleaders]TikTok[/url], and wishlist Ringleaders on Steam!

notes.title: Raising the stakes on social deduction games.
notes.content:
[i]We've just launched our Discord community! [url=https://discord.gg/a9kgTHbJKC]Join us[/url] to view development progress updates and be the first to hear about our playtests.
[/i]

[h1]The Game Design of Ringleaders[/h1]

This post is designed to give an overview of the core game loop for Ringleaders, including our inspiration for the game, and where we plan to take it from here.

In its simplest form, Ringleaders is a social deduction shooter. We love video games like Among Us and Town of Salem, and tabletop games like Secret Hitler and Coup. They make for interesting (and often heated) moments, emergent gameplay, and are the perfect way to spend time with friends, either IRL or online. However, we felt there was a big opportunity to incorporate engaging action gameplay in addition to the social deduction mechanics.


[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44532630/bdf3aaa956c66f61b0b289345ea8495ae138bd8f.png[/img]

In order for Ringleaders to capture the heart of social deduction combined with skill-based progression, we knew it had to have some key components:

[h2]Proximity Voice Chat[/h2]
In-game voice chat is an important layer that puts the “social” in social deduction. We think a lot more social deduction games should have some kind of voice chat baked into the game, so that was one of the first features we implemented. And not just general team chat — proximity chat specifically. This creates many interesting opportunities to be deceitful, and makes it feel like you’re really inside the city of Carillon (where Ringleaders takes place).

[h2]Action Gameplay[/h2]
Another thing we felt was missing from the modern social deduction landscape was skill-based gameplay, so we placed precision gunplay at the core of our experience. This social deduction game will put your sharpshooting skills to the test!

[h2]Opportunity for Different Play Styles[/h2]
Before each game, players choose two weapons and two gadgets to bring into combat for each round. These weapons range from the short range burst damage shotgun, to a long range sniper rifle, and even a katana if melee is your style. Gadgets range from boosts for things like damage output and speed, a shield, heal, bombs, turrets, and door hacks.

[h2]Limited Map Information[/h2]
We decided not to have a minimap in order to keep players on their toes, and to maximize the need for communication. Social deduction is way more fun when you have to rely on team comms for information.

[h2]Randomized Environments[/h2]
To keep things interesting and varied, we’ve implemented randomization in our maps. Long term, we’d love to integrate more procedural content to maximize the uniqueness of every map and every play session.

[h2]Playtime Doesn’t End at Death[/h2]
There’s nothing less fun then entering a game with your friends, only to die quickly and be stuck with nothing to do while your teammates finish out the game. In Ringleaders, we’re attempting to solve this by letting players “reboot” into enemy sentries, where they then have the option to help or hinder the team.

[h2]Persistent incentives[/h2]
In Ringleaders, we’ve implemented a bounty system, which has big implications for how each game is played. It is meant to serve as a social correction mechanism, where players can use the rewards they earn in game to increase the chances of putting a big target on an opponent’s head. We also give players the option to reward teammates for great plays or good behavior. There’s a lot to unpack here, so we’ll share more details on that later in a dedicated post.


[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44532630/32819a979e1de90e56416d447dfe22b218294371.png[/img]

We’re continuously testing Ringleaders as we develop the game, so a lot of the exact implementation is subject to change. These core mechanics provide a solid rundown of how we are structuring the game, but we have so many exciting features in the queue that we haven’t announced yet, and can’t wait to share with you.

Have any ideas for your dream social deduction game? Have thoughts on our formula? Let us know! We’d love your feedback.

Want to be one of the first playtesters? [url=https://discord.gg/a9kgTHbJKC]Join our Discord[/url] and Wishlist us on Steam so you don’t miss an update:
